rfi.title: Paris balls cancelled amid heatwave as 14 July marks 10 years since Nice
rfi.description: Bastille Day firefighters' balls in Paris and the surrounding suburbs have been cancelled owing to record-high temperatures affecting the capital and most of France, as emergency workers remain on alert. Celebrations begin on Monday, with Paris having brought forward its annual fireworks display by a day to avoid clashing with commemorations marking the 10th anniversary of the Nice attack of 14 July 2016.

rfi.title: France, Germany, UK condemn Iran attacks as renewed fighting with US puts peace deal at risk
rfi.description: The foreign ministers of France, Germany, and Britain have condemned Iran's attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and on countries in the region, as Iran and the United States have traded attacks in recent days, casting doubt on their interim agreement to end the war.

rfi.title: Mbappé, Dembélé, Olise dazzle up front but Maignan makes it possible
rfi.description: France's attacking trio - Kylian Mbappé, Ousmane Dembélé and Michael Olise - have dominated the World Cup headlines, scoring plenty of goals and dazzling fans with skilful moves and fast breaks past opposing defences. Meanwhile, at the other end of the pitch, goalkeeper Mike Maignan has laid the foundation that's made all that attacking flair possible.

rfi.title: Ukraine's allies gather in Paris as Kremlin dismisses 'coalition of warmongers'
rfi.description: Allies of Ukraine gathered in Paris on Monday alongside President Volodymyr Zelensky to reaffirm their support for Kyiv and step up pressure on Russia, at a summit of the so-called "Coalition of the Willing" that the Kremlin promptly dismissed as a meeting of leaders who "do not want peace".

rfi.title: France to summon Russian ambassador over cyber attacks
rfi.description: France will summon the Russian ambassador to Paris over an alleged Russian cyberhacking campaign against European countries including France, as the EU and Britain targeted Russia with coordinated sanctions.

rfi.title: Record 128 migrants cross Channel in one boat as overall numbers drop
rfi.description: A small boat carrying 128 people has reached the coast of England, marking a new record for the largest single crossing of the Channel on a small boat, even as the number of crossings has dropped in recent months.

rfi.title: Experts to deliver verdict on EU social media controls for children
rfi.description: An expert committee is due to deliver its recommendations on Monday on how the European Union should regulate children's access to social media, including a potential blanket ban. More than 20 countries worldwide, including France, have already implemented or proposed age restrictions.

rfi.title: Massive fire burns in Fontainebleau near Paris
rfi.description: Firefighers are mobilised in the Fontainebleau forest south of Paris to contain a major fire that started Sunday and has since forced the evacuation of residents in the area and shut down a major highway at the start of a busy summer holiday travel weekend.

rfi.title: Trump lifts Turkey sanctions, eyes F-35 sale
rfi.description: US President Donald Trump made headlines this week at the Nato summit in Ankara by declaring an end to all sanctions against Turkey, paving the way for the sale of the F-35 stealth fighter jet to the alarm of Greece and Israel.

rfi.title: Champagne, Comté and croissants in the crossfire of climate change, experts warn
rfi.description: France's June heatwave saw temperatures in Paris hit 41C, the same average as Dubai. Experts now say that, in order to adapt to climate change, the country will have difficult choices to make when it comes to its famed lifestyle.

rfi.title: Spain braced to face France's firepower in World Cup semi-final
rfi.description: Spain will attempt to neutralise one of the most potent attacking arsenals in World Cup history on Tuesday when they take on France in a heavyweight semi-final showdown.

rfi.title: China's missile test overshadowed by Iran war, but Pacific nations are watching
rfi.description: China recenly test-fired a nuclear-capable missile from a submarine into the Pacific, the first such launch from a nuclear-powered vessel and the first submarine-based test since 1982.

rfi.title: France remembers 'old demons' of antisemitism on first annual Dreyfus day
rfi.description: Sunday saw France observe its first annual day of commemoration for Alfred Dreyfus, a Jewish army officer wrongly convicted of treason in one of the country's most notorious cases of antisemitism. With reports of hate speech on the rise, President Emmanuel Macron said France had yet to shed its "old demons" of prejudice.

rfi.title: In Zimbabwe, community seed banks are reviving indigenous crops
rfi.description: Zimbabwean farmers are reviving drought-resistant traditional crops through a community seed bank, helping them cope with worsening climate variability. The initiative, rooted in indigenous knowledge, is strengthening food security and offering a safety net against future droughts and floods.

rfi.title: China's rising foie gras industry has France looking over its shoulder
rfi.description: China has risen rapidly to become the world's second-largest producer of foie gras, but producers in France say they are not yet worried about losing their long-held dominance of one of the country's best-known delicacies.

rfi.title: Heatwave forces Tour de France to shorten stage for first time
rfi.description: Tour de France organisers have shortened Sunday's stage by 30km due to extreme heat, the first time in the history of the cycling race that high temperatures have forced a change to the route.

rfi.title: Argentina struggle past Switzerland to set up semi-final showdown with England
rfi.description: Defending champions Argentina needed two goals in extra time to subdue Switzerland 3-1 on Saturday night and advance to a semi-final clash against England.

rfi.title: Norway boss Solbakken rues bad luck in World Cup defeat to England
rfi.description: Norway head coach Stale Solbakken rued his side's bad luck with refereeing decisions during their quarter-final defeat to England on Saturday.

euronews.title: Summer skiers head to melting glacier as heatwave grips France
euronews.description: Hundreds of skiers headed to the Grande Motte glacier in Tignes to escape France's heatwave and enjoy summer skiing. But visitors and experts say the glacier is shrinking rapidly, with scientists warning it could disappear within 10 to 15 years.

euronews.title: World Cup 2026 sticker swap draws thousands for Guinness World Record attempt
euronews.description: Thousands of football fans gathered in Mexico City's Zócalo to swap 2026 World Cup stickers as part of a Guinness World Record attempt. The Panini event brought together collectors of all ages, turning the hunt for missing stickers into a celebration of football, family and community.

euronews.description: Azerbaijan's president also told the Shusha Global Media Forum that long-term gas contracts were needed for Baku to expand production, and said that Baku was considering leaving the Council of Europe.

euronews.title: Hungarian parliament removes President Tamás Sulyok from office
euronews.description: Hungary's parliament has approved the 17th amendment to the constitution. Prime Mİnister Péter Magyar says this is a key step that will allow 'Orbán's political puppets' to be replaced.

euronews.title: Full ban on Israeli settlement trade gets ‘most support’ from EU countries, Kallas says
euronews.description: EU foreign ministers overwhelmingly backed clamping down on EU trade with Israeli settlements during closed-door discussions on Monday, with an official source saying the biggest cohort of countries supported passing new measures without requiring the unanimous backing of all member states.

euronews.title: UK joins EU's €90 billion loan for Ukraine with promise of 'fair' contribution
euronews.description: London has agreed to join in the long-in-the-making EU plan to give Ukraine a much-needed financial boost.

euronews.title: Trump reimposes US blockade and demands 20% Hormuz shipping fee
euronews.description: Trump declared the US would collect a 20% fee on all Hormuz cargo as "Guardian of the Strait," flipping the script on Iran's own toll demands, while US forces struck dozens of targets in Iran and the IRGC hit Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait and Oman in the biggest exchange since the April ceasefire.

euronews.title: Portuguese plane delivers medicines to Venezuela
euronews.description: The cargo includes over eight tonnes of medicines for victims of the two 24 June quakes. The flight also marks the resumption of air links between the countries, halted after the tremors.

euronews.title: Nine European countries and Ukraine form anti-ballistic missile coalition
euronews.description: The creation of the anti-ballistic missile coalition comes in the wake of a growing threat of ballistic missiles on Europe. The declaration states the coalition serves in a 'purely defensive' manner.

euronews.description: The Qatar-Mexico Year of Culture uses art, film, food and football to strengthen cultural ties long after the 2026 World Cup.

euronews.description: The EU has sanctioned VK Company for aiding the repression of critics of President Vladimir Putin and his war against Ukraine. The company says its services remain "available to users as normal".

euronews.title: Prime Minister-to-be Andy Burnham ranks his favourite bands
euronews.description: Andy Burnham has blind-ranked his favourite British bands in a recent interview, giving the public further insight into his listening habits.

euronews.title: Bitter rivalries and golden boots: A ‘line-up for the ages’ in the World Cup semifinals
euronews.description: With four previous champions, Mbappé vs. Yamal, Messi vs. Kane plus an all-star race for the golden boot, the France vs. Spain and England vs. Argentina semifinals have the potential to produce two more World Cup classics.

euronews.description: The phrase “eso sí, sin franceses” in a column by Mariano Rajoy has sparked criticism from the Spanish government and French politicians, who call it racist. The former prime minister insists his words have been taken out of context.

euronews.title: Greece's famous ‘Shipwreck Beach’ to be extended to save its iconic wreck
euronews.description: Plans to extend Zakynthos' iconic Navagio Beach by 30 metres aim to preserve its rusting shipwreck for future generations, as visitors continue to be barred from the popular island attraction because of safety concerns.

lemonde.description: Le chef de l’Etat doit prononcer son dernier discours aux armées, lundi, alors que ses deux mandats auront été marqués par une hausse spectaculaire du budget de la défense et un basculement stratégique majeur face aux nouvelles menaces.

lemonde.title: Des traces d’acétamipride et d’autres néonicotinoïdes dans le Nutella et des miels importés
lemonde.description: Un rapport de l’association Agir pour l’environnement avec l’Union nationale de l’apiculture française, publié lundi 13 juillet, révèle une contamination très inférieure des miels français par ces insecticides interdits, que le Sénat veut réautoriser dans le projet de loi d’urgence agricole en discussion.

lemonde.title: La diplomatie américaine impuissante face à la reprise des hostilités au Moyen-Orient
lemonde.description: Durant le week-end des 11 et 12 juillet, Washington a de nouveau bombardé la République islamique, après l’annonce par Téhéran de la fermeture du détroit d’Ormuz, qu’il entend contrôler. Les frappes américaines ont entraîné des répliques iraniennes.

lemonde.title: Sam Neill, célèbre pour son rôle dans « Jurassic Park », est mort
lemonde.description: L’acteur néo-zélandais, disparu à 78 ans, est aussi bien resté dans les mémoires pour avoir échappé aux vélociraptors dans « Jurassic Park » que pour son rôle de mari du personnage incarné par Holly Hunter dans « La Leçon de piano ».

lemonde.title: France-Espagne : pourquoi les Bleus se sont surnommés « Les méchants » à la Coupe du monde 2026
lemonde.description: Les défenseurs Maxence Lacroix et Ibrahima Konaté ont expliqué que les Tricolores étaient « dans un état d’esprit de gagne » avant d’affronter l’Espagne, mardi 14 juillet, à Dallas (Texas), en demi-finale du Mondial.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : des attaques de drones ukrainiens font quatre morts dans la région de Moscou

lemonde.title: Etats-Unis : l’administration Trump multiplie les procédures judiciaires contre des journalistes

lemonde.description: Annoncée dimanche par les autorités, la maîtrise du sinistre a permis le retour progressif de centaines d’habitants évacués, certains ayant pu regagner leur domicile dès la nuit de samedi à dimanche. Le bilan des victimes pourrait encore évoluer.

lemonde.title: Nos albums coups de cœur : Sasha Stychkina, Vince Staples, DJ Seinfeld, Slift…

lemonde.title: Les frais de saisies sur compte prélevés par les banques alourdissent le budget des plus modestes
lemonde.description: Les commissions perçues en cas de saisies-attributions et de saisies conservatoires sont librement fixées par les établissements.

lemonde.title: Dans le Cher, l’art du clown contre le fléau de la « mort sociale »
lemonde.description: « La France buissonnière ». Deux artistes, Léontine et Octavio, se rendent chez les plus fragiles pour briser leur isolement d’un rire salvateur et résilient.

lemonde.title: En Allemagne, le président, Frank-Walter Steinmeier, estime que la fonction protocolaire du chef de l’Etat doit évoluer face à la montée de l’extrême droite
lemonde.description: « L’impartialité ne suffit plus, il faut prendre position », a affirmé le président allemand, soulignant qu’ « une part non négligeable » des électeurs outre-Rhin « ne vote ni pour le bien ni pour le mal, ni pour la gauche ni pour la droite, mais contre le système démocratique ».

lemonde.title: Au Festival d’Avignon, des artistes en appellent à Emmanuel Macron : « Les coupes budgétaires nous obligent à crier, tant il y a urgence »
lemonde.description: Dimanche, neuf artistes du théâtre, de la danse, du cirque et de la performance, entourés par une quarantaine de créateurs, ont lu un texte adressé au chef de l’Etat devant les 2 000 spectateurs de la Cour d’honneur du Palais des papes.

lemonde.title: « Insolation », d’Emilia Pardo Bazan, roman du tiraillement entre désir et bienséance, fit scandale dans l’Espagne du XIXᵉ siècle
lemonde.description: L’écrivaine, importatrice du naturalisme zolien dans la littérature espagnole et célèbre en son temps (1851-1921), parle un peu d’elle-même dans ce roman d’une jeune veuve passionnée.

lemonde.title: Le Royaume-Uni débloque 250 millions de livres pour protéger la communauté juive après une série d’attaques antisémites
lemonde.description: D’une durée de trois ans, le plan prévoit notamment un renforcement de la présence policière autour des synagogues et des écoles juives, en particulier à Londres.

france24fr.title: En direct : troisième nuit consécutive de frappes contre l'Iran, Trump n'exclut pas un accord

Donald Trump a tout de même estimé qu'un accord avec l'Iran était encore "possible". Avant cela, il avait annoncé le rétablissement du blocus des ports iraniens – prévu mardi à 20 h GMT, selon l'armée. Les Émirats arabes unis ont par ailleurs fait état d'attaques de missiles iraniens contre deux tankers dans le détroit d'Ormuz, faisant un mort. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Donald Trump prononcera un "discours à la Nation" jeudi en pleine reprise des hostilités avec l'Iran

france24fr.title: États-Unis : une juge annule l'accord d'immunité fiscale de Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Un accord passé entre Donald Trump et l'administration fiscale américaine (IRS) permettait au président américain, sa famille et ses entreprises de bénéficier d'une immunité fiscale rétroactive. La juge Kathleen Williams, saisie par 35 anciens juges fédéraux, a décidé lundi de révoquer cet accord, estimant que la plainte initiale du président américain avait été déposée "dans un but inapproprié".

france24fr.title: Ukraine : Coalition des volontaires, quel lever d'action ?
france24fr.description: C'est à l'Hôtel des invalides à Paris qu'Emmanuel Macron a réuni ce lundi la coalition des Volontaires. Alors que la guerre en Ukraine est entrée dans sa cinquième année, les alliés de Kiev ont réitéré leur soutien et même amplifié leur aide militaire en annonçant la livraison prochaine de plusieurs armements. 9 pays européens ont également annoncé la création d'une alliance de défense aérienne contre la menace balistique russe.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026: la fédération sénégalaise explique les raisons du départ de Pape Thiaw
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal c'est l'heure comptes après l'élimination controversée des Lions de la Teranga à la Coupe du monde 2026. france24fr.title: Aux États-Unis, un agent de l'ICE tue par balle un Colombien de 26 ans
france24fr.description: Un homme identifié comme un Colombien de 26 ans a été tué lundi dans le Maine par un agent de l'ICE, l'agence américaine chargée de mettre en œuvre la politique de répression de l'immigration de Donald Trump. Deux groupes de défense des droits humains ont indiqué que l'homme était autorisé à travailler aux États-Unis.

france24fr.title: Ukraine à l’honneur et sécurité renforcée : ce qu’il faut savoir du défilé du 14-Juillet
france24fr.description: Un important dispositif policier sera déployé mardi à Paris et en région parisienne pour sécuriser le défilé militaire du 14-Juillet, le dernier sous la présidence d'Emmanuel Macron. L'événement intervient dans un contexte particulier : en pleine canicule et le jour de la demi-finale de la Coupe du monde entre la France et l'Espagne.

france24fr.title: Bombardements en Iran : Attention à ces photos publiées par Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Ces derniers jours sur les réseaux sociaux, Donald Trump n’a pas arrêté de commenter les nouvelles frappes américaines sur l’Iran allant même jusqu’à diffuser plusieurs photos. Problème : ces clichés ne sont pas récents et ont été retouchés par intelligence artificielle.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : qui pour succéder à Pape Thiaw à la tête des Lions de la Teranga ?

france24fr.title: La transformation locale des minerais critiques africains au cœur d'un sommet à Abidjan
france24fr.description: L'Afrique veut transformer davantage de ses minerais sur son sol, plutôt que de les exporter à l'état brut. france24fr.title: Réunion de la coalition des volontaires à Paris : unis face à la menace russe ?
france24fr.description: Ce lundi se tient à Paris une réunion de la coalition des volontaires. E. Macron a réuni les représentants de 37 pays, en présence de Volodymyr Zelensky. Cette rencontre vise à marquer un « réveil stratégique » de l'Europe face à la Russie et aux États-Unis, selon le président français, qui a prononcé ce matin son traditionnel discours aux armées. La France et les Européens sont prêts à défendre "la liberté et le droit", "au prix du sang s'il le faut", a affirmé Emmanuel Macron.

france24fr.title: La forêt de Fontainebleau encore en feu

france24fr.title: Sécheresse et canicules : "C'est au niveau des territoires que les solutions pourront émerger"

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis peurent la mort de Lindsey Graham : Trump salue "un des plus grands"
france24fr.description: Salué en Europe pour son soutien à l'Ukraine, l'influent sénateur américain Lindsey Graham, décédé soudainement à l'âge de 71 ans, a été salué par Donald Trump comme "un des plus grands". Correspondance de Matthieu Mabin depuis Washington.

phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Warwick and the University of Colorado Boulder have directly observed, for the first time, four white dwarfs in binary star systems in our nearby region of space. phys-org.title: Hidden in Maya wall writings: A named astronomer emerges from 1,200-year-old calculations
phys-org.description: Researchers have reconstructed and transcribed a mathematical formula from the site of Xultun, Guatemala, revealing the name of a Maya astronomer for the first time. During the Classic period (250–900 CE), mathematics and astronomy were a key part of Maya society, with complex calculations based on calendar dates and astronomical observations influencing everything from the erection of monuments to the inauguration of kings and queens.

phys-org.title: Climate disclosure gives Canadian companies an edge with European investors, new research shows
phys-org.description: Canadian companies that disclose their climate-related risks and impacts have a considerable advantage over those that don't when it comes to attracting financing from European institutional investors, according to our recent report for the Institute for Sustainable Finance at Queen's University.

phys-org.title: Floating-electron catalyst withstands week in air while making ammonia under milder conditions
phys-org.description: A surface electrene, BaSiN2:O, developed by researchers at Science Tokyo enables efficient ammonia synthesis under mild conditions while overcoming the long-standing air instability of electrene materials. Synthesized by doping barium silicon nitride with oxygen, the material forms a stable layer of freely floating electrons on its surface.

phys-org.title: Carbon storage could curb more than 90% of AI data center emissions, study finds
phys-org.description: As artificial intelligence accelerates demand for computing power across the U.S., a new study co-authored by Hon Chung Lau, adjunct professor in the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering at Rice University and founder of Low Carbon Energies LLC, has found that carbon capture and storage could play a major role in limiting the climate impact of data centers.

phys-org.title: Scientists uncover molecular mechanism linking water-saving irrigation to cadmium accumulation in rice
phys-org.description: Water-saving irrigation practices, including intermittent irrigation, are essential for sustainable rice cultivation amid growing freshwater shortages. However, periodic drainage creates aerobic soil conditions that drastically boost cadmium (Cd) bioavailability, leading to severe grain Cd enrichment. Disentangling the relationship between water conservation and high grain Cd has been a critical challenge for rice breeders and soil scientists worldwide.

phys-org.title: AI-powered electronic nose can distinguish tens of thousands of odors
phys-org.description: A research team has presented a roadmap for developing an "artificial olfactory system" that detects odors like the human nose and analyzes them using artificial intelligence (AI) by leveraging metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). phys-org.title: Where mainshocks strike may explain earthquake size patterns better than timing, data suggests
phys-org.description: Japan is well known for its large earthquakes, but not all regions show the same patterns of earthquake activity. One way to understand which places tend to experience large or small earthquakes is the b-value, a key statistical measure long used by researchers to understand seismicity and assess earthquake occurrence patterns.

phys-org.title: Six massive landslides discovered on icy Pluto
phys-org.description: Scientists have detected evidence of landslides on Pluto for the first time. A paper published in the journal Icarus reports that images taken by the New Horizons spacecraft during a flyby revealed six large landslides in three impact craters.

phys-org.title: New imaging method reveals how electric fields reshape ferroelectric materials
phys-org.description: New research is shedding light on longstanding debates over the behavior of ferroelectric materials when those materials are exposed to electric fields. The findings stem from the use of a novel technique that allows researchers to observe the real-time behavior of domain walls in ferroelectric materials as they are "poled" and "depoled."

phys-org.title: Hidden barriers keep many Californians from coast, survey reveals

phys-org.title: Scientists and citizens are more persuasive than government and industry in mobilizing action, study finds
phys-org.description: In environmental, health and technology crises, Americans are more persuaded to take action by scientists and public consensus than by leaders in government and industry, according to a study in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences by researchers at Boston College and Princeton University.

phys-org.title: Why climate scientists need to talk more about the very worst‑case scenarios
phys-org.description: London is underwater. The Houses of Parliament, Buckingham Palace, St Paul's Cathedral and the Bank of England are all submerged. Far away, the West Antarctic and Greenland ice sheets have collapsed, triggering accelerated sea-level rise which, combined with a storm surge in the North Sea and a high spring tide, has led to water flooding over the Thames Barrier. Thousands of shops, offices, schools and houses are several feet deep in effluent-rich water.

phys-org.title: 'Silly sprinklers' put in reverse to further unravel decades-old physics puzzle
phys-org.description: Each summer, lawns are marked by a familiar addition: "silly sprinklers," whose loops and spirals spew water in creative ways. While seemingly frivolous in their construction, a team of mathematicians has used their design to address a long-standing mystery surrounding the laws of physics.

phys-org.title: New 3D thermal cloak hides objects from heat in any direction
phys-org.description: Researchers have designed and built the first 3D device that can make objects invisible to heat, an advance that could transform how we protect sensitive electronics, manage heat in microchips and shield equipment from thermal detection.

undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: The Mother of All Economic Shocks Is Chinese Mercantilism
proj-syn.description: Because analysts tend to put the United States at the center of the global economic story, they have overlooked the single most important force of the past 50 years. But it will be obvious to later generations that Chinese mercantilism has been more globally consequential than any other economic shock or policy choice.

proj-syn.title: Letting Russia Burn
proj-syn.description: From relentless Ukrainian drone strikes to soaring inflation and fuel shortages, Russia is paying an ever-higher price for Vladimir Putin's war of choice. But the war has become the organizing principle of Putin’s regime, leaving no path to lasting peace without a fundamental political transformation.

proj-syn.title: What AI Governance Demands
proj-syn.description: AI governance must account for everything from the technology’s material requirements to its effects on communities, businesses, labor markets, the environment, and strategic competition. To this end, a framework of verification-based trust—broader than national regulation and more flexible than a classic treaty—is essential.

proj-syn.title: A Japanese Wake-Up Call for America
proj-syn.description: Japan’s deepening currency and bond-market woes should be a wake-up call for other countries that appear to be on unsustainable fiscal paths, not least the United States, as well as France, Italy, and the United Kingdom. After all, a crisis in one country often draws investors' attention to others facing similar problems.

proj-syn.title: The Israel-Lebanon Recipe for Never-Ending War
proj-syn.description: Lebanon’s political circumstances, together with Iran’s strengthened regional position, make Hezbollah’s complete disarmament highly unlikely. By conditioning Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanon on this outcome—but with no provisions about cutting Hezbollah’s Iranian lifeline—the new framework agreement is dead on arrival.

proj-syn.title: Why This Energy Shock Is Different
proj-syn.description: Unlike recent energy crises, today’s geopolitical shock is destroying supply rather than rerouting it, exposing the limits of the standard policy toolkit. Governments can mitigate its impact on those most exposed, but only if fiscal and monetary policy work in concert.

proj-syn.title: China’s Erasure of Tibet Is Accelerating
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the international community has stood idly by while China has systematically eradicated Tibetan culture and identity. With the authorities stepping up their assimilation efforts, Asia risks not only losing one of its oldest civilizations, but also facing a China that is bigger, bolder, and more powerful than ever.

proj-syn.title: Judging the Enhanced Games
proj-syn.description: If fairness in sports required a level playing field that all who wish to compete could afford, that would be a reason for banning expensive performance-enhancing drugs. But it would be a reason for banning expensive high-tech swimming suits and expensive high-tech running shoes, too.

proj-syn.title: What Is the Digital-Money Debate Really About?
proj-syn.description: Both the US and Europe are moving to create digital money, but neither has the right idea about how to do it. The key is to allow “narrow banks,” which issue money but not credit, to keep their reserves in central banks and provide capped interest payments to coin holders.

proj-syn.title: An Athenian View of American Democracy
proj-syn.description: At 250, America is now producing a mindless, raw power and exponentially growing instability. The possibility of catharsis that characterized the United States at its bicentennial is hard to envisage a half-century later—to the detriment of us all.

proj-syn.title: Low-Cost Solutions to Maternal Mortality Already Exist
proj-syn.description: As foreign aid declines, policymakers in lower-income countries must increasingly focus on making better use of scarce resources. When it comes to maternal mortality, that means investing in simple, proven, and affordable interventions for postpartum hemorrhage, pre-eclampsia, and obstructed labor.

proj-syn.title: Postmodern Economics
proj-syn.description: Eschewing the idea of a single truth, the recently deceased English artist David Hockney showed that the world unfolds before us in ways we cannot fully understand. After long clinging to the pretense of certainty, economists would do well to embrace the same insight.

proj-syn.title: Digital Public Infrastructure Is Now a Strategic Battleground
proj-syn.description: Digital identity platforms, payment systems, and data exchanges promise more efficient, inclusive, and responsive public services. But in an era of geopolitical rivalry and concentrated digital power, those same systems create strategic dependencies that governments can no longer afford to ignore.

proj-syn.title: Should the Bank of Japan Raise Interest Rates?
proj-syn.description: At the beginning of 2013, when "Abenomics" was rolled out in Japan, the yen was significantly overvalued, and looser monetary policy was badly needed. Today, the opposite is true, indicating that interest-rate hikes may well be the right prescription for Japan.

proj-syn.title: How Argentina Can Protect Its Resource Wealth
proj-syn.description: Alaska, Norway, and Chile recognized the economic and political risks that accompany commodity booms and established sovereign wealth funds to preserve their resource revenues. Argentina’s hydrocarbon- and lithium-rich provinces should learn from their experience.

proj-syn.title: Reinventing Development Finance
proj-syn.description: Faced with shrinking concessional finance and rising borrowing costs, Rwanda has worked with the World Bank Group to leverage limited public funds and risk-sharing instruments to unlock private capital at scale and on affordable terms. It's an arrangement holding important lessons for low-income countries that must do more with less.

proj-syn.title: Mamdani’s American Dream
proj-syn.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Independence Day address was a perfect example of ideology in the positive sense of the term. It overturned both the right-wing populist narrative of the United States and the left-wing "woke" critique with a vision that has the potential to mobilize a majority.

proj-syn.title: How Vulnerable Are US Financial Markets?
proj-syn.description: Fueled by more than $1 trillion in borrowed money and rising leverage across the financial system, US stock markets may have entered bubble territory. Two developments could trigger a sharp correction: higher interest rates and a loss of confidence in the handful of tech giants driving the AI boom.
